title: Levenda's archival assessment of MJ-12 and his talk with Stanton Friedman
summary: Peter Levenda tells of Levenda's archival assessment of MJ-12 and his talk with Stanton Friedman, about 1940s-1950s documents; conversation at Contact in the Desert at Washington, D.C., and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: National Archives / Library of Congress; Contact in the Desert

tellings.quote: Those documents to me look real.

plain: A researcher, Peter Levenda, talks about the MJ-12 documents, a set of papers said to date from the 1940s and 1950s that describe a secret group called Majestic 12. He says that after looking at them against records in Washington, at the National Archives and the Library of Congress, the documents look real to him, and he says he discussed them with a man named Stanton Friedman at a gathering called Contact in the Desert. If the papers are genuine, a secret group of officials would have been handling UFO matters at the highest level.
